excerpt: Wave is a mobile money service in Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire and other African markets: free deposits, withdrawals and bill payments, and transfers for a 1% fee.
content:
Wave is a mobile money app for people in Francophone West Africa and other African markets. Users deposit and withdraw cash through a network of agents, pay bills, buy airtime and send money to other people from their phone. Its website says deposits, withdrawals and bill payments are free and that sending money costs 1%.

Wave grew out of Sendwave, a remittance company that Drew Durbin and Lincoln Quirk founded in 2014 and that WorldRemit later bought, TechCrunch reported. Wave's own about page names Durbin as cofounder and CEO and says its mission is to make Africa the first cashless continent. In September 2021 Wave raised a $200 million Series A at a $1.7 billion valuation, jointly led by Sequoia Heritage, Founders Fund, Stripe and Ribbit Capital, which TechCrunch called the largest Series A in the region; at the time Wave said it was the largest mobile money player in Senegal. In July 2022 it cut about 15% of its staff, TechCrunch reported. In mid-2025 TechCabal reported a $137 million debt round led by Rand Merchant Bank with British International Investment, Finnfund and Norfund.

Wave earns money mainly from its 1% transfer fee rather than subscriptions; there is no paid plan. Fees and availability can differ by country, so check the app in your market. Wave competes with operator-run services such as Orange Money and MTN MoMo, and its low transfer fee is the main reason people switch.

We have not used Wave for this page. It brings together Wave's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
